title: React reads analytics through useAnalyticsQuery plus the specialized useDriveAnalytics and useDocumentAnalytics hooks
content:
There are two tiers, and the difference is how much analytics-path vocabulary leaks into your component.

**Raw tier** — `useAnalyticsQuery` from `@powerhousedao/reactor-browser/analytics` takes the same `AnalyticsQuery` the engine takes: luxon `DateTime` bounds, an `AnalyticsGranularity`, and `select`/`lod` maps keyed by dimension name with `AnalyticsPath.fromString(...)` values.

```tsx
const { data, isLoading } = useAnalyticsQuery({
  start: DateTime.now().minus({ days: 7 }),
  end: DateTime.now(),
  granularity: AnalyticsGranularity.Daily,
  metrics: ["DriveOperations"],
  select: { drive: [AnalyticsPath.fromString(`ph/drive/${driveId}`)] },
  lod: { drive: 1 },
});
```

**Friendly tier** — `useDriveAnalytics` and `useDocumentAnalytics` from `@powerhousedao/common/drive-analytics` take plain strings and a different time vocabulary: `filters` (`driveId`, `operation`, `actionType`, `documentId`, `target`, `branch`, `scope`), `from`/`to` as ISO strings, `granularity`, and `levelOfDetail` instead of `lod`. They build the paths for you and delegate to `useAnalyticsQuery`.

The second argument of `useAnalyticsQuery` is where live updating lives. Pass `{ sources: [AnalyticsPath.fromString(...)] }` and the query refetches when new series land at or under that source; add `refetchInterval` for polled monitoring. Without `sources` the result is a one-shot read.

Both tiers return the standard query-state shape (`data`, `isLoading`), and `data.rows[].dimensions` is what you read to label a chart — e.g. `row.dimensions.find(d => d.name === "actionType")?.path`.

Provenance: draft `04-Reference/04-Processors/_07-DriveAnalyticsHooks.md`; hooks confirmed to exist at `packages/reactor-browser/src/analytics/hooks/analytics-query.ts` and `packages/common/drive-analytics/{useDriveAnalytics,useDocumentAnalytics}.ts` at 6.2.2-dev.45.
description: useAnalyticsQuery takes a raw AnalyticsQuery with AnalyticsPath select and lod; the @powerhousedao/common/drive-analytics hooks take plain-string filters plus from/to and levelOfDetail.
